title: A Laconic Answer
author: James Baldwin
summary: 斯巴达人用一个词“如果”回敬马其顿国王的威胁。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: Many miles beyond Rome there was a famous country which we call Greece. The people of Greece were not united like the Romans; but instead there were several states, each of which had its own rulers.
paragraphs.zh: 离罗马许多英里之外，有一个著名的国家，我们称之为希腊。希腊人不像罗马人那样统一，而是分成好几个城邦，各有各的统治者。

paragraphs.en: Some of the people in the southern part of the country were called Spartans, and they were noted for their simple habits and their bravery. The name of their land was Laconia, and so they were sometimes called Lacons.
paragraphs.zh: 这个国家南部的一些居民被称为斯巴达人，他们以生活简朴、勇敢善战而闻名。他们所在的地区叫拉科尼亚，因此有时也被叫作拉科尼亚人。

paragraphs.en: One of the strange rules which the Spartans had, was that they should speak briefly, and never use more words than were needed. And so a short answer is often spoken of as being laconic; that is, as being such an answer as a Lacon would be likely to give.
paragraphs.zh: 斯巴达人有一条奇怪的规定：说话要简短，绝不用多余的词。因此，简短的回答常被称为“拉科尼亚式”的回答，意思就是拉科尼亚人可能会给出的那种回答。

paragraphs.en: There was in the northern part of Greece a land called Mac; and this land was at one time ruled over by a warlike king named Philip.
paragraphs.zh: 希腊北部有一个地方叫马其顿，那里曾由一位好战的国王腓力统治。

paragraphs.en: Philip of Macedon wanted to become the master of all Greece. So he raised a great army, and made war upon the other states, until nearly all of them were forced to call him their king. Then he sent a letter to the Spartans in Laconia, and said, "If I go down into your country, I will level your great city to the ground."
paragraphs.zh: 马其顿的腓力想成为全希腊的主宰。于是他召集起一支大军，向其他城邦开战，直到几乎所有的城邦都被迫尊他为王。然后，他给拉科尼亚的斯巴达人送去一封信，说：“如果我进入你们的国家，我就把你们的伟大城市夷为平地。”

paragraphs.en: In a few days, an answer was brought back to him. When he opened the letter, he found only one word written there.
paragraphs.zh: 几天后，回信送到了他手中。他打开信，发现上面只写了一个词。

paragraphs.en: It was as much as to say, "We are not afraid of you so long as the little word 'if' stands in your way."
paragraphs.zh: 这等于是在说：“只要‘如果’这个小小的词挡在你前面，我们就不怕你。”
